annotations.title: Apply your classification rules to the whole IFC model

description:
Turn what you read in the overview into rules the tool replays on
EVERY piece of the model, including the ones you were never shown.

THIS IS HOW THE TOOL LEARNS A MODEL. read_ifc_overview gives you some
fifty groups — one per object type, not one per piece. You answer with
RULES on those groups, and this tool applies them to the three thousand
pieces. You never give a verdict piece by piece: the result stays
deterministic because a program, not you, does the matching.

THEN READ THE ANSWER BACK, AND EXPECT TO POST AGAIN. The answer gives
every group with the role your rules gave it and how many pieces that
is. A rule that is too wide shows up on one line — « Gaine
rectangulaire cadree, 471 pieces, centrale_de_traitement_d_air » is a
rule that turned every duct into an air handling unit. Narrow it and
post again. Calling this tool costs nothing and may be repeated as
often as you need.

WHAT NEEDS A ROLE, AND WHAT DOES NOT. Plain ducts and fittings need
none: they are network by nature, and the answer marks them
segment_ou_raccord so you can see at a glance whether a rule caught
them by mistake. What needs a role is everything else — air handling
units, fans, fire dampers, balancing dampers, silencers, louvres,
diffusers — plus whatever must be kept OUT of the network, such as
access zones, equipment plinths or damper motors.

ORDER THE LIST YOURSELF, most specific first, down to the most
general.
The fire damper rule must come before the balancing damper rule, or
« damper » takes everything. Equipment must come before terminals:
« VEN_MSF_MONOBLOC_SIMPLE_FLUX_REPRISE » contains « reprise », and a
return-diffuser rule placed first would claim the air handling unit.

Pieces no rule catches are simply listed, with no warning and no
failure: the engineer judges on the 3D view, not on a coverage report.
